title: Semiconductor Devices — 40 MCQs
description: Covers the p-n junction, semiconductor diode characteristics in forward and reverse bias, full-wave rectification, and logic gates (NOT, OR, AND, NAND, NOR).

questions.q: A p-n junction is formed by
options: joining a p-type and an n-type semiconductor
questions.explanation: A p-n junction is created at the interface between a p-type and an n-type semiconductor region.

questions.q: In a p-n junction under forward bias
questions.explanation: Forward bias reduces the potential barrier, allowing majority carriers to cross the junction.

questions.q: In a p-n junction under reverse bias
options: the barrier potential increases and depletion layer widens
questions.explanation: Reverse bias increases the barrier height and widens the depletion region, resulting in a very small reverse current.

questions.q: The ideal diode in forward bias acts as a
questions.explanation: An ideal diode has zero resistance when forward biased and conducts freely.

questions.q: The ideal diode in reverse bias acts as an
questions.explanation: An ideal diode has infinite resistance when reverse biased and does not conduct.

questions.q: A full-wave rectifier converts
options: low voltage AC into high voltage AC
questions.explanation: A full-wave rectifier produces output during both half-cycles of the AC input, giving pulsating DC.

questions.q: The Boolean expression for an AND gate is
questions.explanation: The output of an AND gate is high only when both inputs are high: Y = A · B.

questions.q: The Boolean expression for an OR gate is
questions.explanation: The output of an OR gate is high when either or both inputs are high: Y = A + B.

questions.q: The Boolean expression for a NOT gate is
questions.explanation: A NOT gate inverts the input: Y = A̅.

questions.q: The output of a NAND gate is high when
options: at least one input is low
questions.explanation: NAND is the complement of AND; its output is low only when both inputs are high.

questions.q: The knee voltage for a silicon diode is approximately
questions.explanation: Silicon diodes begin to conduct appreciably around 0.7 V in forward bias.

questions.q: The knee voltage for a germanium diode is approximately
questions.explanation: Germanium diodes have a lower barrier potential of about 0.3 V.

questions.q: In the reverse-bias characteristic of a diode the current is of the order of
questions.explanation: Reverse saturation current is typically a few microamperes until breakdown.

questions.q: The efficiency of a full-wave rectifier is higher than that of a half-wave rectifier because
options: it uses both half-cycles of the input
questions.explanation: Full-wave rectification utilises both positive and negative half-cycles, giving higher average output and efficiency.

questions.q: The output frequency of a full-wave rectifier for a 50 Hz AC input is
questions.explanation: Each half-cycle produces a pulse, so the output ripple frequency is twice the input frequency.

questions.q: The truth table of a NOR gate shows output high only when
questions.explanation: NOR is the complement of OR; output is 1 only when both inputs are 0.

questions.q: A p-n junction diode is used as a rectifier because
options: it conducts in both directions equally
it conducts only in one direction
it has high reverse resistance and low forward resistance
questions.explanation: The diode’s unidirectional conduction property (low forward resistance, high reverse resistance) makes it suitable for rectification.

questions.q: In a full-wave bridge rectifier the number of diodes used is
questions.explanation: A bridge rectifier employs four diodes arranged in a bridge configuration.

questions.q: The depletion region of a p-n junction contains
options: immobile ions and is depleted of free carriers
both free electrons and holes in equal number
questions.explanation: The depletion layer is formed by diffusion of carriers and is left with immobile space charge.

questions.q: If the inputs of an AND gate are A = 1 and B = 0, the output is
questions.explanation: AND requires both inputs high for output high; 1 · 0 = 0.

questions.q: If the inputs of an OR gate are A = 0 and B = 0, the output is
questions.explanation: OR output is 0 only when both inputs are 0.

questions.q: The Boolean expression for a NAND gate is
questions.explanation: NAND is the negation of AND: Y = (A · B)̅.

questions.q: The Boolean expression for a NOR gate is
questions.explanation: NOR is the negation of OR: Y = (A + B)̅.

questions.q: Zener breakdown occurs in a diode when
options: reverse bias exceeds a certain critical voltage
questions.explanation: Zener (or avalanche) breakdown takes place under sufficiently high reverse bias.

questions.q: The dynamic resistance of a diode in the forward-bias region is
questions.explanation: In the conducting region the slope dV/dI is small, corresponding to low dynamic resistance.

questions.q: In a full-wave rectifier using a centre-tapped transformer the peak inverse voltage (PIV) across each diode is
questions.explanation: Each diode must withstand the full secondary voltage of the other half, i.e., 2 V_m.

questions.q: The ripple factor of a full-wave rectifier is approximately
questions.explanation: For a full-wave rectifier the ripple factor γ ≈ 0.48.

questions.q: The maximum efficiency of a full-wave rectifier is
questions.explanation: Theoretical maximum efficiency of a full-wave rectifier is 81.2 %.

questions.q: A silicon diode has a forward voltage drop of 0.7 V and carries a current of 20 mA. The power dissipated in the diode is
For an ideal full-wave rectifier with peak input voltage V_m the average output voltage is
questions.explanation: V_avg = 2 V_m / π for a full-wave rectifier.

questions.q: The output of a two-input NAND gate is low only when
questions.explanation: NAND output is 0 exclusively when A = B = 1.

questions.q: Which gate is called the universal gate?
questions.explanation: NAND (and also NOR) can implement any Boolean function and is therefore universal.

questions.q: The combination of gates that produces the same output as a single NOR gate is
questions.explanation: NOR = NOT (OR), i.e., an OR gate followed by a NOT gate.

questions.q: In a reverse-biased p-n junction the minority-carrier current is called
questions.explanation: The small current due to minority carriers under reverse bias is the reverse saturation current.

questions.q: If both inputs of a two-input NOR gate are connected together, the resulting gate behaves as a
questions.explanation: When A = B the NOR output is A̅, which is the NOT function.

questions.explanation: By De Morgan’s theorem (A + B)̅ = A̅ · B̅.

questions.q: In a centre-tapped full-wave rectifier each diode conducts for
questions.explanation: Each diode conducts only during one half-cycle of the AC input.

questions.q: The output of the combination of an AND gate followed by a NOT gate is the same as that of a
questions.explanation: AND followed by NOT realises the NAND function.
